{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the framing of the dictator game (giving vs. taking) would have asymmetric effects on the allocation behavior of male and female dictators, specifically that males would be more selfish in the taking frame compared to the giving frame, while females would be more egalitarian in the taking frame compared to the giving frame.",
  "design": "between",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Dictator game frame (Giving vs. Taking) and dictator gender.",
  "outcome_measure": "Amount of money allocated to the recipient (in the giving frame, the amount given; in the taking frame, the amount not taken).",
  "population_and_setting": "Students at the University of East Anglia, participating in a laboratory experiment.",
  "sample_size_total": 140,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via ORSEE; participants received a £3 show-up fee plus earnings from the game.",
  "analysis_plan": "Mann-Whitney tests and OLS regressions to compare allocations across frames and genders, and Probit models to analyze the frequency of selfish (allocating 0) and egalitarian (allocating half) choices.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used a balanced pool of 70 male and 70 female dictators across two treatments. The decision space was £10 in both frames. A second part of the experiment involved recipients guessing the dictator's allocation, but this was payoff-irrelevant to the dictator."
}
